builds.title: Dark theme, several reasons for a slow day, safer date changes and one back button
builds.summary: Supervisors: a slow day can have several reasons, not one (tap each that applies: the note writes itself from your choices, in your language, and you can change it; tap "Rewrite from my choices" to get the written note back). Update and Today now lead with the pieces made, then what was added today in one quiet line, then what is left; after Send the line says what you added ("Saved: 120 pieces added to today, with a note"). A day with no output can be sent as 0 with a reason; "12,5" is no longer read as 125; the number field is not hidden under the top bar on a short screen; a bad photo no longer leaves "Photo ready" beside an error; after a lost reply the phone says "trying again" and retries within seconds; signing out with updates waiting asks first; "Stitching" and "Printing" have Tamil on every screen (draft words, unreviewed). Merchandisers: the order page timeline fits the screen with the ex-factory line in view; Add an update refuses more than the whole stage and asks once before accepting more than is left; moving the ex-factory date asks first and refuses a date more than two years ahead or a year back, and the history shows the year; Cancel link, Back to normal on a closed day and Hide from buyer ask first; search finds colour; Review shows every reason a supervisor chose, the first marked "Main reason", and says when a note was written from those choices. Everyone: a dark theme you choose from the menu (light stays the default: the floor reads these screens in daylight); the same back control on every page; stricter rules for passwords and for characters in names and PO numbers; photos whose hidden data cannot be read are refused; sign-in tries are counted per address and account, so one person's wrong tries do not lock a whole factory out; a strict browser security policy; and an audit report with a plan of action (audit/AUDIT-04-user-perspective.md, audit/POA-AUDIT-04.md).

builds.title: Final check before submission: a safer shared demo, steadier AI suggestions, and fixes across the app
builds.summary: The hosted demo now protects itself from its own visitors: its logins never lock, accounts, buyer links and templates cannot be changed, photos are limited, and the seeded notes and warnings come back every day. The AI suggestions can no longer be called without limit, wait when the service is busy, never show more than 100 percent sure, and keep their English draft within the limit. The app now shows why an order form was refused, opens a new buyer link pasted into a tab that is already open, tells a person when their sign-in has ended, offers the Tamil switch only to supervisors, gives every page its own title, and can be installed with its own icon. The demo password is no longer shipped in a normal build, and a long list of wording, documentation and clean-up fixes went in.

builds.title: Safer and cheaper to run: a bug round on the backend, faster updates, and photos without location data
builds.summary: After every update the server now recomputes only the order that changed instead of every order, so sending an update and opening the board are much quicker and cheaper to run. A long audit found and fixed dozens of small bugs: a stage exactly on pace could show red, a warning could be emailed to a buyer twice, a mistyped date far in the future could freeze the server, a blank purge value could delete every rejected photo, and sign-in revealed which phone numbers have an account. Photos are stripped of camera and location data before they are stored, two people changing the same ship date at once no longer garble its history, and a wrong storage address is refused at start-up. Pages that people reload every minute are now compressed and sent only when they changed.

builds.title: A calm violet look, status stamps, a dashboard for merchandisers and a bolder Today for supervisors
builds.summary: Supervisors: Today opens with a ring and "N of M updated today", then one large card per stage showing the pieces made against the pieces planned and one big Update button; the Update screen has larger numbers, a plain "left", and a back button shaped like the menu button; the sync chip is marked for a moment when it changes ("3 waiting" to "All sent"); the Update screen fits in Tamil at the largest phone font and at 200% zoom; a "page not found" screen with a way back, in Tamil for supervisors; a "Skip to main content" link as the first stop for the keyboard (the Tamil wording of both is a draft, unreviewed); when there is nothing to update the screen says that new orders appear when the merchandiser sets them up; a ring shows straight away when the app starts on a slow connection, and Today shows grey blocks while its list loads. Merchandisers: the board's status filter is a row of tiles with the number in each and the pieces short; each order's progress bar on the board is now by pieces of the current stage ("Sewing: 1,750 of 4,550 pieces"), says so in words when nothing is reported yet, and labels an estimate; search, sort, buyer, unit and ship week sit in one toolbar and a very long buyer name no longer stretches a row; "Don't show" on a warning still waiting for review can be undone in the page (a confirmed warning cannot); cancelled and expired buyer links are folded away; an order opens with tiles for quantity, ex-factory date (with the weekday), stages done and projected finish, with the timeline and the stage cards side by side; Change date is no longer a second filled button; the review headings are clearer; the status page shows the day and time zone and a way back; a new order shows a dash, not a zero, until a size has a number; Setup opens on a pilot checklist and has one Add a person form and a list of account activity. Everyone: every order status is drawn as a ruled stamp (icon, word and colour, no coloured fills); the app has one soft violet theme; form errors are no longer red but dark with a drawn "!"; piece counts are written one way (1,750 and 1,25,000); a date field reads its date back in words.

builds.title: Supervisors keep Send in reach, and merchandisers get tabs and a phone-friendly board
builds.summary: On a phone, a supervisor's Send button now stays at the bottom of the screen, above the keyboard, so it is always in reach once the number is typed. The sign-in opens on the form that phone used last (a phone already in Tamil opens the supervisor form), shows Tamil and English side by side, and a button that cannot be used yet is a clear grey. Today says how many of the day's stages have an update and which date the counts go to, and after a send the next stage is one tap away. Merchandisers get Board, Review and Setup as tabs on every screen, with the number waiting for review always in view. The People table keeps its words whole, and on a phone the board's filters sit behind one Filters button, so the first order appears much higher. This build also carries the board, order and Setup improvements made since build 1006 that were not yet released.

builds.title: Set up the pilot: people, holidays, templates, and a lost phone in one click
builds.summary: A merchandiser can now add supervisors and merchandisers (easy PINs like 1234 are refused), reset a PIN, sign someone out on every phone at once, or stop an account, and it takes effect on the very next request. Units, closed days for each unit (Deepavali, a shutdown, an extra day worked) and the stage lists used to schedule orders can all be set up from a Setup screen. An approved photo can be withdrawn from the screen, and the files of old rejected photos can be cleared. If two supervisors share a phone, one person's waiting updates are never sent under the other's sign-in, and the screen says so.

builds.title: Say why a stage is slow: a reason and a note, in Tamil or English
builds.summary: A supervisor can now add to a daily update a reason (one tap from a short list: not enough workers, workers on leave, machine problem, material late, no power, fixing quality, something else) and a few typed words in Tamil or English. They travel with the update, even with no signal, and arrive exactly once. A merchandiser reviews each note in the review queue, adds the English meaning of a Tamil note and checks the reason; notes also appear on the order's page. Notes are internal and never shown to buyers. An update can now only attach a photo that really belongs to that order.

builds.title: A photo with the daily update, and a steadier daily rate
builds.summary: A supervisor can add a photo to a daily update. The phone shrinks it first (a large camera picture becomes roughly 150 KB) and sends it with the update, even after a lost signal or a lost reply, without ever making a duplicate. A merchandiser approves or rejects it in the review queue, and a buyer sees only approved photos of their own orders. Separately, the daily rate is now worked out from completed days, so a small update sent in the morning no longer drags a late-risk order's rate down and raises a false warning.

builds.title: Nothing reaches a buyer until you confirm it, and a buyer sees only their own orders
builds.summary: Warnings about at-risk stages now wait in a review queue. A merchandiser reads the wording a buyer would see (kept free of internal figures), can reword it, then confirms it or hides it; changing a stage's colour needs a fresh look. Merchandisers can make a private link for one buyer contact, set how long it works, and cancel it. The buyer opens it with no sign-in and sees only their own orders, planned dates and confirmed warnings, read-only. A link opens nothing else, and a missing, unknown, cancelled or expired link all give the same message.

builds.title: Set up an order and see exactly why it has its colour
builds.summary: Merchandisers can create an order from a form and see, before creating it, the date each stage must finish, worked backwards from the ex-factory date. Opening an order from the board shows each stage with the planned finish date beside the date it will really finish at the current rate, how far apart they are, the progress and the working behind the colour. The ex-factory date can be changed there; a reason is required and every change is kept in a history showing who, when, what and why.
